job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: The aroma of sizzling spices drifted through the busy lanes of Lajpat Nagar as Raju set up his small food stall. It was 4:00 PM, and the evening rush was just beginning. Raju, a man with a quick smile, had been running this stall for 12 years. His specialty, the spicy aloo-tikki, was famous among the local shopkeepers. Suddenly, a young boy named Rohan ran up, breathless, asking for a plate. Rohan had been playing cricket at the nearby park and was famished. Because the oil in the pan was extremely hot, the tikkis turned golden brown in only three minutes. A lady named Mrs. Sharma walked by, complaining that the smoke was making her eyes water. Raju apologized politely, explaining that the high heat was necessary for the perfect crunch. By 6:30 PM, Raju had sold out of his entire stock, leaving only a few crumbs on the metal tray. He wiped his brow, satisfied with the day's earnings, and started packing his cart to head home.
response.summary: Raju runs a popular street food stall in Lajpat Nagar that attracts many hungry customers. He uses high heat to cook his famous aloo-tikkis quickly. By the end of the evening, he successfully sells all his food.
